newsitem.title: UK: Firstbus climbs on talk of govt bus plans.
newsitem.headline: Firstbus climbs on talk of govt bus plans.

text.p: Shares in UK transport group Firstbus Plc gained on Wednesday after a report in the Financial Times said the government would disclose plans to encourage motorists to use buses instead of cars, dealers said.
Firstbus shares climbed 11p, or 5.47 percent, to 212p by 0812 GMT, making them the best performer in percentage terms in the top 350 UK stocks.
The newspaper report said the government would use a "carrot and stick" approach with new powers being handed to local authorities to promote bus travel.
The proposals, which the newspaper said would be announced on Wednesday, could also involve higher car parking charges and road tolls to discourage people from using their cars.
Dealers said a 52 page "buy" note on Firstbus by analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson had also added upward momentum to the shares.
Analysts at Kleinwort said its note highlighted the possible changes to the regulation of bus transport and presented a similar argument to the newspaper report.
